ITEM.context_text: You see a group of students talking to each other during registration. How would you interact with them?
The Facilitator called you for your turn during registration. He tries to engage in small talk with you.
Your roommates are talking late at night about the official schedules starting tomorrow. One said, "I can’t wait for the opening ceremony tomorrow!"
A facilitator walks down the crowded queue, holding up a massive stack of orientation brochures, and asks: "Could someone with some energy please help me hand these out to the rest of the queue?"
You look around your Mahallah Cafe holding your food, looking for a place to sit. The only open spot is next to a group of laughing seniors.
You return from the washroom to find someone has taken your seat, despite your belongings being there. What do you do?
Early morning at the sports complex, facilitators blast upbeat music and asks everyone to follow along to their aerobics routine.
Your facilitator splits everyone into small usrah circles. The microphone is finally passed to you for your introduction.
Your team is completely stuck on ideas for your group chant. You have a concept that could help out your group.
Your facilitator is asking for every group to elect a leader. Do you let others take the charge or will you lead?
Your roommates are arguing whether to put your shoes and slippers inside or outside the room. What do you do?
A final montage is played after the Bai’ah Ceremony. It is a compilation of everyone’s activities and events that happened throughout the week.
In the packed SHAS Mosque Foyer queue for RHB card activation, a student barges in right in front of you and a pale, dizzy Haris. What do you do?
After the Murabbi Session, a tiny, shivering stray kitten mews beneath a stone bench by the mosque walkway. Maghrib is close and Haris looks exhausted.
Ten minutes before the Insan Madani session, a freshman in the Kulliyyah courtyard stares at their phone map, close to tears — they're at the wrong block.
The ambulance is on its way. How are you feeling right now?

CARD_OPTION.dialogue_text: I'll quietly stay far away from them and focus on my own things.
I'll sit near the group, but keep to myself unless one of them speaks to me.
I'd sit nearby and listen to their conversation, waiting for a natural moment to offer a comment.
I would walk up, introduce myself quickly, and ask if I could join their discussion.
I will join in, introduce myself loudly, and be very friendly and outspoken.
Engages enthusiastically, tells a lot about your life and journey, and asks multiple follow-up questions.
Answers, shares one piece of light personal information, and asks a simple return question.
Answers politely with a neutral, short response.
Gives a brief, one-word answer and immediately returns focus to the registration process.
Just a simple nod and agree.
Absolutely! I've been looking forward to starting university life for months!
Yeah, it sounds pretty exciting. Can't wait to see the campus crowd.
It's fine, probably just another standard assembly.
Not really. It's probably just going to be hours of formal speeches.
Honestly, I feel completely indifferent about it. I just want this week to be over.
Pretends not to hear the question, focusing entirely on a phone/the ground.
Shakes head subtly and avoids eye contact, hoping someone else volunteers.
Looks around to see if anyone else is stepping up, but doesn't move.
Politely offers to help the facilitator distribute the brochures for the small area nearby.
Immediately calls out, takes the entire stack, and walks up and down the queue energetically handing them out.
Hey guys! I couldn’t help but be interested in what you’re laughing about. May I join you?
Hello, is this seat taken? Thanks. (Sits down and offers a polite smile)
(Sits down quietly without making eye contact, focusing on your meal)
(Hesitates, feels awkward, and looks for an emptier table at the far corner instead)
(Completely avoids the crowded hall and decides to eat back in your dorm room alone)
Quietly find another seat far away, assuming you must have been gone too long.
Wait near the seat, hoping the person notices your belongings and offers to move.
Politely ask, "Excuse me, I think this was my seat? No worries if you need it, but I left my book here."
Directly say, "Pardon me, I was sitting here. Can I please have my seat back?"
Assertively state, "You took my seat. My belongings are right here, please move now."
Go to the front row and move along with maximum energy.
Follow along with decent energy and a positive attitude.
Performs basic movements at a neutral pace.
Follow slowly, doing the bare minimum to participate.
Stands still at the back, waiting for the routine to end.
Hi. Nice to meet everyone.
Hello everyone. I'm here to study at IIUM. It's great to meet you all.
Hi. I'm looking forward to getting involved in campus life. I also enjoy a few hobbies. Glad to be here.
Hey guys! I love meeting new people and I'm excited about starting this journey. Let's definitely connect outside of this usrah!
What's up everyone! I'm generally pretty outgoing, so don't hesitate to say hi. I can't wait to get to know all of you! Who's next?
Listen up everyone! I have the perfect cheer idea that will definitely win us the prize. Let’s do it!
I think my idea could work really well if we try doing it together.
Here's an idea, it's okay if you guys want to use it or not.
I have a small suggestion... but it's fine, if you guys don’t want it.
(Keeps the concept to yourself entirely, assuming the group will ignore your input anyway)
Let me be the leader. I’m the best one here.
I'll step up to lead, if there are no objections.
I'm okay with leading, but we should hold a vote.
I don't mind, I'll follow whoever wants to step up and lead.
I’m not very good at leading. I’ll pass on this.
I suggest we put it to a group vote. I'm happy to go with whatever the majority decides.
I'll state my preference calmly, then step back and let the others discuss and decide.
I intervene immediately and suggest a compromise that respects both sides.
I clearly state what I think is the most logical solution and give reasons why it should be adopted.
I settle the argument immediately by confidently stating the final rule: 'We're doing it this way, end of discussion.'
This is dragging on. When is this ever going to end?
I guess that was okay, but when can we leave?
A nice summary, definitely a decent way to end the week.
That was enjoyable! It was quite heartwarming.
That was fantastic! I’m so glad I came. (Claps enthusiastically)
Look down at your shoes and let him cut in silently, hoping the line still moves fast enough for Haris.
Sigh audibly and whisper to Haris that people have no manners, waiting to see if the booth staff notices.
Tap the student's shoulder gently: "Excuse me bro, the end of the queue is back there—my friend isn't feeling too well."
Step forward clearly: "Hey, we've been waiting our turn for half an hour and my friend needs to sit down soon. Please queue at the back."
Call him out loudly in front of the whole line and demand he step out of the queue immediately.
Keep walking past without slowing down; campus cats fend for themselves and you don't want to be late.
Feel a pang of pity and pause for a second, but decide someone else with actual cat food will probably help it later.
Share a small piece of the bread/bun in your bag, leave it on a napkin, and hurry back to the Mahallah.
Kneel down calmly, break up your snack and pour clean drinking water into a bottle cap for the kitten while asking Haris to sit on the bench and rest for five minutes.
Sprint to the nearest kiosk/convenience stall to buy proper wet food for the kitten and gently move it to a dry, sheltered corner before heading back.
[Use Cat Food from Inventory] Open the pouch of cat treats and feed the kitten right here, while Haris catches his breath on the bench.
Avoid eye contact and slip into your lecture hall quickly; approaching a stranger alone makes your chest tighten.
Hover nearby hoping a committee facilitator spots them so you don't have to speak up.
Wait until the student looks your way, then point them toward the main directory signboard with brief directions.
Walk over gently, ask which Kulliyyah they're looking for, and pull up the campus map together to show them the exact shortcut.
Reassure them warmly, text Haris to save your seat, and personally walk the student halfway to the neighboring Kulliyyah corridor so they don't get lost again.
My heart won't stop pounding; I feel sick with dread.
[DRAFT] My heart is racing and my hands are shaking, but I'm trying hard not to fall apart.
[DRAFT] I'm shaken, but I'm holding on and keeping an eye on Haris.
[DRAFT] I'm still rattled, but steady enough to keep Haris calm and focused.
Terrified, but I had to keep a level head for Haris.
